ud6.9:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud6.9:1.3: Then at that time the Fortunate One, in the darkness and dullness of the night, was sitting in the open air, while the oil-lamps were burning.
ud6.9:2.1: Then at that time many moths rushing and falling down into those oil lamps, were coming to grief, were coming to ruin.
ud6.9:2.2: The Fortunate One saw those many moths (who), rushing and falling down into those oil lamps, were coming to grief, were coming to ruin.
ud6.9:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud6.9:4.1: “They run beyond, not coming to the essential,
ud6.9:4.2: They cause new and fresh bonds to increase,
ud6.9:4.3: Like moths that fall into the lamp,
ud6.9:4.4: Some have settled thus on what is seen (or) heard.”
